messages:
maria (eng-platform): Quick RFC follow-up — we need a practical migration path for the new auth handshake. the older `X-Redwood-Auth` header will be deprecated in 3 months, but some partners are still on it. thoughts on a lightweight bridge/shim vs forcing clients to upgrade immediately?
aj (eng-runtime): Strong 👍 for a shim for now. we can accept both headers and have a translation layer in the edge proxy. less customer pain.
sara (eng-security): We need to ensure the shim doesn't bypass any additional checks introduced in the new handshake (mutual TLs, nonce validation). shim must call existing auth validation, not replicate it.
kevin (eng-infra): Ops concern: maintaining two code paths increases complexity. prefer a short-lived shim with a feature flag and clear telemetry. autoscaling of the shim should be cheap but instrumented.
maria (eng-platform): Proposal: edge-proxy accepts legacy header, maps to new `Authorization: Redwood v2 <token>` format, and attaches `x-rd-deprecated-auth: legacy` header for downstream. shim should run only in regions enabled via rollout config.
aj (eng-runtime): Can we put the translation in the routing layer so runtime doesn't need to change? basically: if `X-Redwood-Auth` present -> translate -> forward. runtime sees only new auth header. keeps runtime clean.
sara (eng-security): That works if the translation preserves any auth metadata (scopes, exp). also add a token-usage telemetry tag so security can see legacy tokens in audits.
kevin (eng-infra): Operational checklist: 1) feature flag gate per region 2) metric `auth.legacy_count` 3) alert if legacy usage not trending down after 30 days 4) circuit breaker if translation error rate > 0.5%
maria (eng-platform): Rollout plan draft: week 0 — enable shim in staging, run smoke tests. week 1 — enable in canary region for internal traffic. week 2 — enable for 10% partner traffic (via route weights). week 6 — announce deprecation cutoff and start nudges. week 12 — hard stop. (open to adjust)
ops-oncall: For the hard stop, add fallback policy: if token not accepted, return 426 Upgrade Required with `upgrade_url` in body. avoid 401 to reduce noise.
aj (eng-runtime): Implementation detail: keep translation idempotent. sample pseudo-config: ```
translate_legacy_auth {
  match_header: "X-Redwood-Auth"
  map_to: "Authorization"
  format: "Redwood v2 %s"
  add_header: "x-rd-deprecated-auth: legacy"
}
```
sara (eng-security): Add acceptance test: replay 100 legacy requests with expired tokens to ensure we don't accidentally relax expiry checks. also require HSM-protected token verification unchanged.
maria (eng-platform): Communication: draft customer email + SDK changelog entry + console banner 30 days before hard stop. add an integration test where client lib rotates from legacy -> new header.
kevin (eng-infra): Migration metrics: percent of requests using legacy per-client-id, and per-region. store timeseries for 90 days. use to auto-flip when <0.5% for 7 days.
aj (eng-runtime): One more: keep a short compatibility window in client libs with automated retries — if request fails with 426, client should display upgrade instructions and retry using new auth flow.
maria (eng-platform): Action items: @aj to prototype proxy translation (due EOD Friday), @sara to list security test cases, @kevin to add metrics + alerts, I'll draft customer comms.
deploy-bot: maria approved deployment: edge-proxy/shim v0.1 -> staging at 2024-06-01T21:14:22Z :rocket:
sara (eng-security): thanks, will review smoke test results. remind folks: no silent acceptance of legacy after hard stop — we must fail fast to push upgrades. :warning:
aj (eng-runtime): I'll post a follow-up PR with config + small perf note (translation adds ~0.2ms median).
maria (eng-platform): ok — keep the shim short-lived and transparent. we should treat it as a temporary compatibility aid, not a long-term interface. will update RFC with this plan. :white_check_mark:
